newsitem.title: MEXICO: Witch planted body in Salinas murder drama.
newsitem.headline: Witch planted body in Salinas murder drama.

text.p: A reputed witch robbed the grave of a distant relative and planted the body on the ranch of ex-president Carlos Salinas' brother, Raul, apparently to incriminate him in a political assassination, authorities said on Friday.

Mexico City Attorney General Jose Antonio Gonzalez said the witch, now a Mexican celebrity known as "La Paca", ordered her son-in-law to dig up his dead father's corpse and re-bury it on the grounds of Raul Salinas' ranch on the outskirts of the city.

On a tip from La Paca, police unearthed the body last October, suggesting it belonged to a congressmen, Manuel Munoz Rocha, whom Raul Salinas is accused of conspiring with to kill a ruling party leader in September 1994.
Munoz Rocha has been missing for more than two years. Mexican authorities admitted earlier this month the body on Salinas' ranch was not his.
Raul Salinas has denied responsibility in the murder case. His lawyers said when the body was dug up that it had been planted to incriminate their client.
Friday's announcement appeared to bolster Raul Salinas' chances of an acquittal in the case. He also faces illicit enrichment charges.
Later on Friday, the federal Attorney General's office issued a statement saying that the results of the investigation do not affect the murder case against Raul Salinas.
"From a legal point of view, there are no procedural ties between the results of the investigation and the case underway against Raul Salinas...," the office of the federal Attorney General said.

Mexico City official Gonzalez said La Paca, whose real name is Francisca Zetina, and seven other alleged accomplices were in jail on Friday on charges including grave robbery and perjury. Some had testified against Raul Salinas.

He also suggested more prominent heads may roll. "The attorney general's office continues investigating the case to determine the suspected involvement of some ex-public servants," Gonzalez told a news conference.
Newspapers have speculated that Pablo Chapa Bezanilla, the former special investigator in the murder case, may be arrested in connection with the discovery of the planted corpse.
Chapa received the tip from La Paca about the body's wherabouts and was present when it was unearthed.
